_note: Demo reference table for 5 states. Summaries are simplified and must be reviewed by HR compliance or counsel before production use. Each rule has an owner-reviewed date; rules older than 12 months are flagged for re-verification.

rules.name: California Paid Sick Leave
rules.summary: Employees accrue at least 1 hour of paid sick leave per 30 hours worked; employers must allow use of at least 40 hours (5 days) per year.

rules.name: California Family Rights Act (CFRA) and Paid Family Leave
rules.summary: CFRA gives up to 12 weeks of job-protected leave to employees with 12 months of service and 1,250 hours in the past 12 months (employers with 5+ employees). State Paid Family Leave provides partial wage replacement for up to 8 weeks.

rules.name: New York Paid Sick Leave
rules.summary: Employees accrue 1 hour per 30 hours worked. Employers with 100+ employees must provide up to 56 hours per year; 5 to 99 employees, up to 40 hours.

rules.name: New York Paid Family Leave
rules.summary: Up to 12 weeks of job-protected, paid leave at 67% of average weekly wage (capped). Eligible after 26 consecutive weeks for employees working 20+ hours a week, or 175 days for those working under 20 hours.

rules.name: Washington Paid Sick Leave
rules.summary: Employees accrue at least 1 hour of paid sick leave per 40 hours worked, with up to 40 unused hours carried over each year.

rules.name: Washington Paid Family and Medical Leave
rules.summary: Employees who worked 820 hours in the qualifying period can take up to 12 weeks of paid family or medical leave (up to 16 combined).

rules.name: Illinois Paid Leave for All Workers Act
rules.summary: Employees accrue 1 hour of paid leave per 40 hours worked, up to at least 40 hours a year, usable for any reason. Chicago and Cook County have their own ordinances.

rules.name: Texas (no state paid sick leave law)
rules.summary: Texas has no statewide paid sick leave requirement; company policy applies.

federal.name: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA)
federal.summary: Up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave per 12 months for eligible employees.
